jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Sequoia Living is seeking an accomplished Executive Director to provide strategic and operational leadership for a senior living community in San Francisco.

The Executive Director has overall responsibility for community operations, resident experience, financial performance, regulatory compliance, workforce leadership, and long-term planning. This individual will lead a multidisciplinary team and work closely with residents, organizational leadership, and community partners to maintain a high quality living and care environment.

The successful candidate will combine strong business and operational judgment with a resident centered leadership approach. This role requires an executive who can build effective teams, strengthen organizational culture, manage complex operations, and successfully navigate the regulatory requirements associated with senior living and healthcare services.

Depending upon community needs and licensing requirements, the Executive Director may serve as the licensed Nursing Home Administrator or fulfill designated administrative responsibilities in accordance with applicable California regulations.

Key Responsibilities

Executive & Operational Leadership
Provide overall leadership and direction for the day-to-day operations of the community.
Develop and execute short and long-term operating plans that support organizational priorities and the evolving needs of residents.
Establish measurable goals and performance expectations across departments and monitor progress against key operational indicators.
Identify opportunities to improve service delivery, operational efficiency, resident satisfaction, and organizational effectiveness.
Lead major initiatives involving programs, staffing, facilities, capital improvements, and community operations.
Partner with organizational leadership and other communities to identify effective practices and implement appropriate operational improvements.
Ensure policies, procedures, and operating practices are effectively implemented throughout the community.

People & Culture
Build, lead, and develop a high-performing, service-oriented leadership team.
Maintain overall accountability for workforce planning, recruitment, hiring, onboarding, training, performance management, employee development, and retention.
Create an environment that encourages collaboration, accountability, open communication, and continuous improvement.
Coach and develop department leaders while establishing clear expectations for performance and service.
Support leadership development and succession planning to strengthen organizational continuity.
Promote positive relationships among employees, residents, families, and organizational leadership.

Resident Experience & Community Relations
Foster a welcoming, engaging, and respectful environment that supports residents' quality of life, independence, dignity, and well being.
Develop strong relationships with residents and resident leadership groups to understand priorities, address concerns, and support community initiatives.
Ensure resident feedback is incorporated into operational planning and service improvements.
Provide leadership related to admissions, occupancy, resident services, and overall community experience.
Maintain productive relationships with families, community organizations, professional partners, volunteers, regulatory agencies, and other external stakeholders.

Financial Management
Provide overall financial stewardship for the community, including annual budgeting, forecasting, financial analysis, and expense management.
Monitor financial and operational performance and implement corrective strategies when necessary.
Evaluate staffing, programs, services, capital expenditures, and operational investments from both financial and resident-service perspectives.
Partner with organizational leadership to develop long-range operating and capital priorities.
Ensure resources are deployed effectively to support operational excellence and long-term sustainability.

Regulatory Compliance, Safety & Risk Management
Maintain compliance with applicable federal, state, and local requirements governing senior living, residential care, and skilled nursing operations.
Ensure appropriate systems are in place to protect resident health, safety, rights, and well-being.
Provide executive oversight of community risk management, loss prevention, emergency preparedness, workplace safety, and accident and illness prevention programs.
Ensure appropriate investigation, documentation, follow-up, and corrective action related to safety and operational concerns.
Maintain readiness for regulatory surveys, inspections, audits, and other compliance reviews.
Promote a culture of quality, safety, accountability, and continuous improvement throughout the organization.

Strategic Leadership & Quality Improvement
Translate organizational priorities into actionable community-level strategies.
Use operational, financial, workforce, quality, and resident-experience data to evaluate performance and guide decision-making.
Lead quality assurance and performance improvement initiatives.
Identify emerging operational challenges and develop proactive solutions.
Participate as a member of the organization's senior leadership structure and contribute to broader strategic initiatives, committees, and special projects.

Knowledge, Skills & Leadership Capabilities

The successful candidate will bring:
Strong knowledge of senior living and/or healthcare operations, including applicable California regulatory requirements.
Working knowledge of Title 22, OBRA, and regulations governing skilled nursing facilities, residential care settings, and services for older adults.
Understanding of California requirements applicable to continuing care retirement communities and/or Life Plan Communities.
Demonstrated ability to lead complex, multidisciplinary operations.
Strong financial acumen, including budget development, forecasting, financial analysis, and expense management.
Proven ability to recruit, develop, motivate, and retain high-performing teams.
Strong communication, relationship-building, conflict-resolution, and organizational skills.
Ability to analyze complex information, assess alternatives and risks, and make sound business and operational decisions.
Demonstrated commitment to serving older adults with dignity, respect, and an understanding of the opportunities and challenges associated with aging.
Ability to successfully balance resident needs, regulatory requirements, workforce considerations, financial objectives, and organizational priorities.

Qualifications
Approximately 8–10 years of progressively responsible administrative and leadership experience, preferably within senior living, healthcare, skilled nursing, Life Plan/CCRC, or a similarly complex service environment.
Significant experience leading multidisciplinary teams and complex operations.
Previous executive or senior-level leadership experience within a senior living environment strongly preferred.
Demonstrated responsibility for financial management, workforce leadership, regulatory compliance, and operational performance.
California Nursing Home Administrator (NHA) license may be required, or the successful candidate must be eligible and willing to obtain the appropriate license based on community requirements.
California Residential Care Facility for the Elderly (RCFE) Administrator Certification may also be required based on the scope of the position.

Supervisory Responsibility
The Executive Director holds overall leadership responsibility for a substantial community workforce and leads operations both directly and through department heads and other managers.

This position has executive-level accountability for workforce strategy, hiring, leadership development, employee performance, organizational culture, regulatory compliance, resident experience, financial performance, and overall community operations.

POSITION DETAILS

”At Baruch College we believe that student success is everyone’s responsibility"

Baruch College seeks the next Director of the Starr Career Development Center. This position will report to the Assistant Vice President for Career and Industry Partnerships in the Division of Academic Affairs in support of the division's values and goals and the College’s mission and strategic plan. The Director will be a change agent and visionary leader, with strong academic credentials and leadership ability in career development, career-readiness and exploration, experiential learning, and employer relations. The Director is responsible for providing innovative, strategic leadership and comprehensive career development services to the college community. They will play a key role in the implementation of the CUNY Beyond and Next Level Student Success initiatives. The Director is a highly visible, engaged professional, who will lead and manage the college undergraduate career center as it supports and assists a diverse student population, alumni, faculty, and employer clients. The Director will oversee services and programs involving the development of career education, career identification and search, and pursuit of employment opportunities commensurate with students’ academic aspirations. The Director will also cultivate a culture of continuous improvement by identifying and integrating best practices; benchmarking services against peer and aspirant institutions; introducing creative approaches and solutions to the design and delivery of programs and services; maximizing available technology for data management, marketing and communication; and actively supporting ongoing professional development and collaborations across staff and functional responsibilities. Starr’s Director will oversee departmental budgets, always ensuring prudent fiscal management and oversight they will also seek external funding sources to augment unit revenue and supplement college funding.

Oversees office’s industry partnerships, establishes new partnerships and nurtures ongoing partnerships
Directs overall operations of physical and virtual career centers, including staff, facilities, and technologies
Seeks external funding sources to augment unit revenue and supplement college funding
Strengthens relationships with Deans, Chairs and faculty to further embed career pedagogy in the classroom. Share student and industry data with forementioned academic partners to inform curriculum and degree programs.
Plans and implements marketing strategies for identifying and cultivating a diverse group of potential employers
Plans, promotes, and markets services and information to students, including information resources, career counseling, informational programs, and assessment programs
Participates in campus committees and projects including but not limited to Accreditation Committees, Curriculum Committees, CUNY Beyond Committees, Next Level Student Success Committees and more.
Contributes to the leadership of the field through conferences, presentations, leadership in professional organizations.
Represent the department and the College to internal and external stakeholders, including employers, donors, media, economic development agencies, and professional organizations

Other Information

Recent institutional analyses as part of Baruch College’s “Next Level Student Success” project have highlighted the need for stronger integration, clearer pathways, and scalable student success practices across the student experience. The Director of the Starr Career Development Center will be expected to engage in this work collaboratively to support the implementation of the College’s vision for an integrated approach to student success and to do so with a strong orientation toward data-informed decision making and continuous improvement.

Baruch College is a selective, urban, public college within CUNY, enrolling a very diverse undergraduate and graduate student body, the majority of whom are Pell-eligible. Baruch is nationally recognized for student outcomes, socioeconomic mobility (#1 nationally), and value (#1 nationally), while also facing the complexities common to large public institutions: scale, affordability pressures, and the need to coordinate student support across multiple organizational units.

CAMBA is a community of staff, volunteers, clients, donors, neighbors and partners who work together to build an inclusive New York City, where all children and adults have access to the resources and supports, they need to thrive. We take a comprehensive approach by offering more than 180 integrated programs in: Education & Youth Development, Family Support, Job Training & Employment Support Services, Health, Housing, and Legal Services. More than half of our clients are immigrants and refugees from around the globe. Over 85% of our families are living in poverty, reflecting the challenges faced by nearly 1.7 million New Yorkers today.

Learning to Work (LTW)
for Transfer Schools will provide services to students, ages 15-21 that are over-aged for grade, under-credited, and have spent at least one year in another high school to earn a high school diploma and gain valuable vocational and life skills supports. Each program has an Internship Developer who works with students to provide meaningful career exploration experiences, including providing an internship experience for all students who are interested.

The Crenulated Company Ltd. dba New Settlement Apartments (“New Settlement”) is a community-led, mission-driven settlement house rooted in the Bronx. For more than 35 years, New Settlement has worked with youth, families, residents, and community members in the Southwest Bronx to build resilience, expand opportunity, and strengthen neighborhoods through after-school education and youth development, workforce development and college readiness, health, fitness, and wellness programming, community organizing for better housing and safer schools, and arts, creative expression, and community-building initiatives.

Rooted in the Bronx, New Settlement stands with community members to break systemic barriers, advance justice, promote leadership, and strengthen neighborhoods. By ensuring agency around education, employment, housing, wellness, and creative expression, New Settlement helps cultivate an equitable society where individuals and families have the power to use their voice to create the change they wish to see.

Position Summary

The Assistant Program Director for After School Programming supports the Program Director in the daily administration, supervision, and delivery of a high-quality DYCD-funded after-school program. The position helps ensure that programming is safe, inclusive, youth-centered, and consistent with the approved DYCD Work scope, program schedule, contractual requirements, and organizational policies.

The Assistant Program Director provides direct supervision and guidance to assigned program staff, monitors participant attendance and engagement, supports curriculum implementation, maintains required documentation, communicates with families and school partners, and assists with continuous quality improvement. In the Program Director’s absence, the Assistant Program Director assumes responsibility for daily site operations and serves as the primary on-site contact.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Program Operations and Compliance

Support the day-to-day operation of the afterschool program, ensuring services are delivered in accordance with DYCD contracts, program goals, enrollment targets, regulatory requirements, and organizational policies.
Monitor program activities, participant supervision, staffing ratios, facility readiness, and daily site operations to ensure a safe, organized, and high-quality program environment.
Assist with program opening and closing procedures, special events, and overall site coordination.
Serve as the primary site leader in the absence of the Program Director, ensuring continuity of program operations, supervision, compliance, and participant safety.
Support compliance with all applicable requirements of DYCD, DOE, DOHMH, OCFS/SACC, and other regulatory agencies.

Program Quality and Youth Development

Support the implementation of engaging, age-appropriate programs that promote positive youth development and incorporate social-emotional learning, literacy and academic enrichment, STEM (science, technology, engineering, mathematics, and arts), physical activity and healthy living, leadership and life-skills development, college and career awareness, and arts, recreation, and cultural enrichment.
Review program plans, conduct observations, and provide coaching and feedback to staff to ensure high-quality instruction and participant engagement.
Support the Program Director in creating opportunities for participants to share their interests, influence program activities, assume leadership roles, and provide meaningful feedback on their program experience.
Foster an inclusive, welcoming, and supportive environment that meets the diverse needs, abilities, identities, and interests of participants, and collaborate with the Inclusion Coordinator and other designated staff to ensure appropriate accommodations and meaningful participation for all youth.
Assist with continuous quality improvement efforts, including corrective action plans, monitoring follow-up, and implementation of program enhancements.

Staff Supervision and Development

Provide supervision, guidance, scheduling support, and daily oversight to frontline staff, interns, and volunteers, ensuring adequate staffing coverage and compliance with required participant-to-staff ratios.
Assist with staff recruitment, onboarding, training, professional development, and performance management.
Monitor staff attendance, preparedness, professional conduct, and compliance with organizational and regulatory requirements.
Support coaching, documentation, and corrective action processes as needed.
Ensure staff understand and adhere to safety procedures, mandated-reporting requirements, and participant supervision expectations.

Participant Engagement, Attendance, and Family Partnerships

Monitor participant enrollment, attendance, participation, and retention to ensure compliance with contractual requirements and achievement of program enrollment and participation goals.
Oversee the accurate collection, review, and timely entry of attendance and enrollment data, regularly monitoring attendance trends, absenteeism, lateness, and participation rates, and addressing discrepancies or areas of concern.
Develop and implement strategies to improve participant engagement, attendance, and retention, including outreach to families, follow-up regarding absences or inconsistent attendance, identification of barriers to participation, and implementation of re-engagement strategies.
Support recruitment, enrollment, orientation, and retention efforts, maintaining accurate enrollment records, participant files, and waitlists, and ensuring enrollment and rate-of-participation requirements are met.
Establish and maintain positive relationships with participants and families by communicating program expectations, attendance requirements, participant progress, upcoming events, and available support services; responding to questions and concerns; and elevating significant issues as appropriate.
Support family engagement initiatives, including orientations, workshops, conferences, celebrations, and other program events that strengthen participant and family connections.
Collaborate with school personnel, community partners, and service providers to support participant success, align program activities with school-day priorities, expand resources and opportunities for participants and families, and facilitate referrals when additional support is needed.
Prepare and share attendance, enrollment, and participation reports with program leadership and recommend strategies to strengthen participant engagement, retention, and overall program outcomes.

Safety, Behavior Support, and Incident Response

Ensure the safety, well-being, and active supervision of participants throughout all program activities, including arrivals, transitions, field trips, special events, and dismissal.
Implement and reinforce positive behavior-management and restorative practices that promote a supportive, inclusive, and respectful program environment.
Respond promptly and appropriately to behavioral incidents, injuries, medical concerns, family complaints, and emergencies, ensuring timely communication with program leadership and required stakeholders.
Ensure incidents are properly documented, reported, and resolved in accordance with organizational policies, DYCD requirements, and mandated-reporting obligations.
Support emergency preparedness efforts, including drills, evacuation procedures, crisis response protocols, and staff training.
Maintain the confidentiality and appropriate handling of participant medical, behavioral, emergency, and accommodation-related information, and support the safe planning and execution of field trips and off-site activities.

Data Management and Administrative Support

Maintain accurate, organized, and confidential program records, including attendance, enrollment, incident documentation, family communications, staff compliance records, and other required program documentation.
Ensure timely and accurate data entry, reporting, and recordkeeping to support contract compliance, program monitoring, audits, licensing reviews, regulatory requirements, and organizational reporting needs.
Assist with administrative and operational functions, including staff scheduling, supply and inventory management, purchasing, timesheet review, and resource allocation.
Support the planning and coordination of special events, field trips, family engagement activities, showcases, and other program initiatives, ensuring alignment with the approved program calendar and established deadlines.
Participate in supervisory meetings, DYCD trainings, technical-assistance sessions, and professional development opportunities, and perform other duties as assigned by the Program Director or department leadership.

Job Description

World Wildlife Fund (WWF), one of the world’s leading conservation organizations, seeks a Managing Director, WWF Impact.

Major Function

WWF Impact is a dedicated investment function effort that sits within the Nature Finance and Investment (NFI) team. The Managing Director will oversee all of WWF Impact’s activities, which include initiating and managing partnerships with external sustainable investment asset managers and managing an evolving portfolio of direct equity investments into start-ups that further our conservation mission. The Managing Director will manage a highly skilled team of conservation investment professionals in pursuit of successful high impact partnerships and private investment opportunities. The Managing Director will serve on the leadership team of the broader NFI team and will have primary responsibility for managing WWF Impact’s relationships, internally and externally in the market.

Key Responsibilities

Leadership and Strategic Direction: Lead WWF Impact, the dedicated team within NFI where we pursue both direct early stage (catalytic) investing opportunities as well as external partnerships with asset manager partnerships in which WWF serves the role of impact advisor.
Asset Manager Partnerships: Oversee the process to forge new asset manager partnership opportunities through effective partner identification, collaboration, diligence, and project / fund development. Work with the WWF Impact team, NFI Management, and WWF programmatic teams to pursue and close high potential asset management partnerships in priority sectors (regenerative agriculture, blue oceans, sustainable infrastructure, circular economy, carbon finance, etc.). Play lead role in negotiating partnerships with potential partners.
Catalytic Portfolio: Oversee the early-stage direct investment portfolio (catalytic investing), including opportunity pipeline review, investment analysis, due diligence / legal process management. Ensure that investment memorandums are well-prepared and uphold a rigorous standard for investment and impact analyses. Lead the investment team in presentations and deliberations in internal governance processes.

Resource Mobilization: Develop, maintain and advance key internal and external relationships for partnership success. This includes funding partnerships with partners (philanthropic & investment), WWF programmatic goal team and global network relationship management, asset manager relationship management, and portfolio company relationships.
Management: Oversee a growing team of professionals within the WWF Impact team. Manage WWF Impact’s budget and build capacity of both WWF US and Country Office staff in support of NFI’s goal of significant capital mobilization to conservation finance.
External Engagement: Represent WWF Impact and NFI at external events, conferences, and workshops. Travel domestically and internationally (up to 25%), to priority landscape regions in Latin America, Asia and Africa.
Collaboration: Collaborate and develop partnerships across geographies and work closely with WWF’s conservation goal teams, country offices, and private sector engagement and development / capital raising teams to advance integrated nature finance strategies.
Other duties as assigned.

Key Competencies

Financial Acumen: Structure and advance innovative impact investments, navigate nuanced and complex decisions, and demonstrate strong deal instincts.
Private Capital Mobilization and Nature Finance Innovation: The Managing Director will advance nature finance innovations through a combination of new structures / design and partnership models.
Executive Presence & Influence: Represent WWF with diplomacy, credibility, and authority while engaging investment managers, investors, donors, corporate leaders, multilateral development banks, development finance institutions, and other senior stakeholders.
Strategic Thinking & Execution: Identify high-impact opportunities, assess complex trade-offs, exercise sound judgment, and deliver results in dynamic, fast-moving environments.
Strategic Partnership Building: Build trusted, long-term relationships and align diverse stakeholders across governments, financial institutions, MDBs, DFIs, private sector actors, and civil society organizations around shared conservation and financing goals.
Resource Mobilization: Secure and structure financial support from public and private sources to advance blended finance initiatives and transaction development objectives.
Global Collaboration: Work effectively across cultures, geographies, and a highly-matrixed global organization, including coordination with other WWF teams, WWF Country Offices and international partners.

Qualifications

Skills and Abilities

Minimum of 15 years of experience in the financial services sector, including private equity, venture capital, impact investing, conservation finance, environmental and conservation-based investing.
Advanced degree from a relevant field, such as finance, business administration, economics, international relations, or political science.
Strong preference for candidates who have worked with or in the field of emerging market private equity in environmental sectors, and have a track record of designing and executing multi-party blended finance solutions.
Demonstrated experience developing and evaluating investment strategies, conducting due diligence, assessing investment opportunities, portfolio management, deal structuring, and the use of capital instruments.
Experience working within or alongside multilateral and bilateral finance institutions, including development finance institutions and development banks, in support of investment structuring, partnerships, or capital mobilization initiatives.
Sector expertise in one or more of WWF’s priority areas (e.g., regenerative agriculture and food systems, blue economy/aquaculture, sustainable infrastructure, or carbon markets), with experience working in Latin America, Africa, Asia, or other emerging markets preferred.
Awareness of key components of sustainable investment, including investment instruments, term sheets, blended finance techniques, deal structuring, etc.
Exceptional written, verbal and presentation skills.
Financial modeling skills and fluency with Microsoft Excel. Able to review, analyze, and evaluate financial models, financial projections, company valuations, etc.
Demonstrated ability to analyze complex problems and to effectively communicate solutions to others.
Competency in a second language (ideally Spanish or Portuguese) a significant plus.
Strong coordination and teamwork and excellent interpersonal skills.
Proven ability to manage and deliver against multiple time sensitive priorities.
A dynamic, creative, and outgoing personality with a commitment to nature conservation.
Committed to building and strengthening a culture of inclusion within and across teams.

COURAGE – We demonstrate courage through our actions, we work for change where it’s needed, and we inspire people and institutions to tackle the greatest threats to nature and the future of the planet, which is our home.

We run two national flagship programs: a six-month virtual intensive for Insurance & Risk Management professionals and a year-long monthly program for Women Lawyers. Regional chapters operate in Cleveland and Seattle.

About FortifyAI

FortifyOS is governance and compliance software for AI agents. It helps enterprises discover agents and control their actions through endpoint, gateway and agent framework integrations.

The platform is built and functional, and we have one signed design partner.

We’re seeking additional companies to help shape the product around real enterprise requirements and establish the foundation for a commercial offering.

* FortifyAI has also been accepted into the NVIDIA Inception program.

Why this problem matters

AI agents access sensitive data, use credentials and take actions across business systems. Enterprises need to know which agents are running, what they’re allowed to do and when a human should approve an action. They also need records for incidents and audits. Foundation labs and platforms are building related safeguards; we expect real competition.

Our focus is enforcing company policy before an agent acts, across models, applications and internally built agents, without sending sensitive activity to an external LLM. We then produce the evidence security and compliance teams need.

Design partnerships will help establish where this approach adds value beyond existing tools and build the customer and investor case for the business.

Who you’ll build with

You’ll work alongside a technical cofounder with more than 25 years of experience building enterprise software and leading engineering teams. His background includes leading a global engineering organization at Apple across AI, security and cloud infrastructure, and senior architecture roles at Cisco and Brocade.

More recently, he acquired an established QA and compliance business and has led its adoption of AI. At FortifyAI, he has led product strategy, architecture and development of FortifyOS.

The CEO role is open because FortifyAI’s other cofounder, currently CEO of an established cybersecurity company, is unable to continue as FortifyAI’s operating CEO. He intends to remain involved as an advisor and investor.

Build the commercial team and partnerships as the business grows.

Experience with early-stage fundraising and the ability to present a credible business case to investors.
Prior founder or early commercial leadership experience.

Comfort with the uncertainty and financial risk of an equity-only opportunity.

We’re especially interested in evidence of the customer commitments you’ve secured and your contribution to raising capital.

This is an equity-only founder opportunity, with no cash salary at this stage. Equity and vesting terms will be agreed as part of forming the partnership.

Founding Director of Operations — Job Description

Taíno CoLAB Academy NH | Opening September 2027 

ABOUT TAÍNO CoLAB ACADEMY 

Taíno CoLAB Academy is a public charter high school opening in New Haven, CT in September 2027. Rooted in the Taíno community's history and New Haven's vibrant Latino heritage, Taíno CoLAB is designed as a Community School 2.0
— genuinely embedded in, accountable to, and in reciprocal relationship with its community. 

Academically, Taíno CoLAB operates through the 4D Quantum Learning Matrix
— CoLAB Education's signature framework for future-ready, student-centered learning across four interconnected dimensions: Inquiry, Design, Creativity, and Service. Students don't just learn about the world — they investigate it, design within it, create across it, and serve through it.  

We are not a traditional school with innovative add-ons. We are a fundamentally different kind of school. We are looking for a Director of Operations who is energized by that distinction. 

THE ROLE 

The Director of Operations of Taíno CoLAB Academy is the school's chief operational and administrative leader
— responsible for translating the CoLAB vision into robust, equitable, and seamless operational systems that support students, teachers, families, and community partners.

This is not a purely administrative desk job. The Director of Operations builds the structural backbone of a learning community
. They work in close partnership with the Founding Executive Director, the Founding Director of Academics, and CoLAB Education's leadership team. Reports to: Executive Director.

SYSTEMS OWNERSHIP 

The Director of Operations owns the following systems — accountable for their design, implementation, and continuous improvement: 

1. Financial Management and Budgeting System

Design and manage the school's operating budget in alignment with strategic priorities. Oversee accounts payable/receivable, payroll processing, grant management, and audit preparation. Ensure financial transparency, compliance with state and federal regulations, and fiduciary stewardship of public funds.

2. Facilities, Safety, and Capital Infrastructure System

Oversee the leasing, design, maintenance, and safety compliance of the school's physical plant. Create a warm, welcoming, and secure physical environment that reflects the school's identity as a community resource. Manage facilities vendors, emergency preparedness drills, security systems, and custodial operations.

3. Technology, Data, and Information Systems

Manage all educational and operational technology infrastructure, hardware deployment, and software licensing. Ensure secure student data privacy compliance (FERPA, state standards). Oversee the Student Information System (SIS) and provide operational data support for enrollment, attendance, and reporting.

4. Compliance, Governance, and Legal Operations

Manage charter accountability reporting, state and federal compliance filings, board operations support, and legal risk management. Ensure adherence to health, safety, nutritional, transportation, and special education compliance frameworks.

5. People Management System

Manage onboarding, benefits administration, credentialing tracking, and HR compliance for all school staff. Support the Director of Academics and Executive Director with recruitment logistics, personnel recordkeeping, and staff culture initiatives from an operational lens.

6. School Operations and Logistics Partnership

Partner with the Director of Academics on daily school operations, student transportation, food service delivery, student registration, and family communications. Ensure operational priorities actively serve instructional goals — never the reverse.

EXPECTED APPROACHES

Lead as a Learner 

The Director of Operations is a chief learner in operational excellence — not an immovable expert. They model curiosity about how systems run, ask operational and front-line staff questions before imposing solutions, and credit the team's ideas. They are the first to test a new process, workflow, or software protocol and the first to reflect on what isn't working smoothly for teachers, students, or families.

Facilitate, Don't Dictate 

The Director of Operations leads through service and collaboration. They listen to the needs of educators and families, using feedback loops to continuously refine operational processes and remove barriers.

Center Community Voice Structurally 

Operations must reflect the community's values. The Director of Operations ensures that families experience welcoming, accessible, and culturally responsive administrative interactions from registration to daily engagement.

Hold Equity as the Core Standard 

The Director of Operations understands that operational equity means resource allocation and service delivery prioritize the students and communities most often underserved by traditional institutions.

Think in 4D 

The framework applies to operations, too. Every operational workflow is evaluated through the lens of Inquiry, Design, Creativity, and Service to ensure the school's infrastructure mirrors its innovative pedagogical model.

Model Adaptive Confidence 

Leading a founding school requires comfort in ambiguity and rapid iteration. The Director of Operations makes sound decisions with incomplete information, communicates transparently about operational hurdles, and embraces mistakes as data points for system improvement.

Requirements And Preferences

The Broward County Board of County Commissioners, Transportation Department
is seeking qualified candidates for the position of
Chief Operating Officer (Assistant Director of Transportation) in its Operations Division.

The Community

Bordering Southeast Florida’s Atlantic coastline, Broward County is the seventeenth most populous county in the nation and the second largest in the state of Florida. Home to over 1.9 million people, Broward County is located between Palm Beach and Miami-Dade counties, forming the center of South Florida’s largest metropolitan area in which 6.1 million people reside. Within the County’s approximate 1,200 square miles are 31 municipalities, the largest of which is the county seat, Fort Lauderdale. About two-thirds of Broward County is part of the undeveloped Everglades conservation area. Broward County boasts 23 miles of pristine Atlantic coastline, and its beaches attract both the local population as well as tourists from around the world. With an average year-round temperature of 76 degrees, Broward County has a tropical climate and is a choice destination for over nineteen million visitors every year.

Broward County’s warm climate, demographic diversity, robust and expanding economy, top-rated schools, colleges and universities, cutting-edge healthcare, and an advanced transportation system afford its residents an exceptional quality of life. Broward offers world-class dining, high-quality theater, cosmopolitan nightlife, and premium shopping venues, as well as an abundance of recreational activities such as golf, pickleball, soccer, deep-sea fishing, boating and vast opportunities for fun on the beach.

The Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport is in Broward County and is less than two miles from Port Everglades where most major cruise lines use as a homeport. Among Broward County’s abundant retail shopping options is Sawgrass Mills, the largest one-story value retail shopping mall in the United States. For the sports enthusiast, Broward County is home to the National Hockey League’s Florida Panthers, while the National Basketball Association’s Miami Heat, the Major League Baseball’s Miami Marlins, and the National Football League’s Miami Dolphins are just a short drive or quick train ride away.

The County Government

The Broward County government was established under Charter in 1975 as a home-rule government. The County has a Council/Manager form of government. The Broward County Board of County Commissioners is composed of nine members, elected every two years for four-year staggered terms. Commissioners are voted to the position by their district constituents through partisan elections. The Mayor and Vice-Mayor are Commission members annually elected by the Commission for one-year terms. The Commission appoints the County Administrator, the County Attorney, and the County Auditor.

The County Administrator serves as the Chief Executive Officer and manages the County’s six major operating departments: Transportation, Aviation, Finance and Administrative Services, Human Services, Port Everglades, and Public Works and Environmental Services; eight offices and three divisions, which all together comprise over 70 lines of business.

The County has nearly 6,700 employees and eight organized bargaining units. The County budget for FY26 is $8.75 billion of which $5.45 billion is Operating, $2.55 billion is Capital and $0.76 billion is Debt Service. The budget reflects strategic investments in transit, the seaport and airport, and many other critical services to residents.

Broward County Department of Transportation

The Broward County Transportation Department is comprised of a comprehensive transportation network that ensures the safe, secure and efficient movement of its citizens.

The existing public transportation network provides approximately 26 million fixed route and express service bus trips annually. In addition, the organization is adding over 200 miles of premium service through its Premium Mobility (PREMO) plan. Under PREMO, BCT is transitioning from a bus only organization to a full multi-modal provider of public transportation with heavy rail, light rail, bus rapid transit, and high frequency bus service thus reducing the reliance on single-occupancy vehicles and helping to alleviate traffic congestion. The integration of these premium public transportation services will ensure seamless connectivity between bus services and other transit options.

BCT works closely with federal, state, and local governments, regional agencies and the community at large to address transportation needs and priorities. Moving forward BCT will have an enhanced level of long-term planning and coordination with the numerous government organizations, such as the Federal Transit Administration (FTA), Federal Railroad Administration (FRA), Transportation Security Administration (TSA), Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), Florida Department of Transportation State Safety Oversight Office and the Broward County Metropolitan Planning Organization. By leveraging federal, state, and local funding, the department is able to implement innovative solutions and infrastructure improvements, enhancing the overall quality of life for Broward County residents.

The Position

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) provides leadership and direction for the Transportation Department's Operations Division, including bus, rail, paratransit, on-board systems, and fleet services. Responsibilities include executive oversight, operational management, financial performance, strategic planning, employee development, safety promotion, customer advocacy, and coordination of assigned division activities. This is a 24/7 operation.

This is an executive leadership position. The incumbent will advise the Transportation Director on strategy, issues, and resolutions. The COO will review and analyze policies, procedures and practices and work with key stakeholders for recommendations/assistance. The COO will be well versed in industry standards and stay abreast of current best practices. Customer service is paramount and special focus must be placed on KPI trends and response. It is critical that the COO develop productive, collaborative relationships with Broward County leaders, Transportation Department leaders, union representatives, employees, customers, and the community. The COO must manage in a manner that ensures Broward County Transportation is viewed favorably by customers and employees.

The incumbent will work under limited direct supervision, leading the development and implementation of programs within organizational policies and reports major activities directly to the Department Director through verbal, written, and virtual communications. The COO must be able to respond to emergency incidents 24/7.

The Ideal Candidate

The COO is an essential member of the BCT senior leadership team. The ideal candidate will have a proven track record of analyzing data and developing solutions to improve performance. This individual will forecast for future resource needs as they relate to the current structure and upcoming PREMO expansion, while developing and maintaining solid relationships with key internal and external partners.

The COO will participate in union negotiations and union/management relations, playing an instrumental role in developing collaborative, professional, and growth-oriented cultures across all levels of the Operations sections.

As a leader grounded in servant and transformational leadership, the selected candidate will foster a nurturing, employee-focused environment centered on staff development and job satisfaction. By actively engaging staff at all levels, the incumbent will ensure every team member feels heard and appreciated. Additionally, the COO will develop strategic plans to advance entry- and mid-level management skill sets, building a robust leadership pipeline from the ground up. This approach supports BCT’s commitment to a Just Culture environment, where mistakes are treated as learning opportunities while team members maintain accountability for their errors.

The COO will collaborate with section leaders to assess current operations for Bus Operations, Bus Maintenance, Paratransit, On-Board Systems, Fleet Services, and Rail to determine immediate and future strategies for optimum performance.

The Crenulated Company Ltd. dba New Settlement Apartments (“New Settlement”) is a community-led, mission-driven settlement house rooted in the Bronx. For more than 35 years, New Settlement has worked with youth, families, residents, and community members in the Southwest Bronx to build resilience, expand opportunity, and strengthen neighborhoods through after-school education and youth development, workforce development and college readiness, health, fitness, and wellness programming, community organizing for better housing and safer schools, and arts, creative expression, and community-building initiatives.

Rooted in the Bronx, New Settlement stands with community members to break systemic barriers, advance justice, promote leadership, and strengthen neighborhoods. By ensuring agency around education, employment, housing, wellness, and creative expression, New Settlement helps cultivate an equitable society where individuals and families have the power to use their voice to create the change they wish to see.

Position Summary

The Assistant Program Director for After School Programming supports the Program Director in the daily administration, supervision, and delivery of a high-quality DYCD-funded after-school program. The position helps ensure that programming is safe, inclusive, youth-centered, and consistent with the approved DYCD Work scope, program schedule, contractual requirements, and organizational policies.

The Assistant Program Director provides direct supervision and guidance to assigned program staff, monitors participant attendance and engagement, supports curriculum implementation, maintains required documentation, communicates with families and school partners, and assists with continuous quality improvement. In the Program Director’s absence, the Assistant Program Director assumes responsibility for daily site operations and serves as the primary on-site contact.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Program Operations and Compliance

Support the day-to-day operation of the afterschool program, ensuring services are delivered in accordance with DYCD contracts, program goals, enrollment targets, regulatory requirements, and organizational policies.
Monitor program activities, participant supervision, staffing ratios, facility readiness, and daily site operations to ensure a safe, organized, and high-quality program environment.
Assist with program opening and closing procedures, special events, and overall site coordination.
Serve as the primary site leader in the absence of the Program Director, ensuring continuity of program operations, supervision, compliance, and participant safety.
Support compliance with all applicable requirements of DYCD, DOE, DOHMH, OCFS/SACC, and other regulatory agencies.

Program Quality and Youth Development

Support the implementation of engaging, age-appropriate programs that promote positive youth development and incorporate social-emotional learning, literacy and academic enrichment, STEM (science, technology, engineering, mathematics, and arts), physical activity and healthy living, leadership and life-skills development, college and career awareness, and arts, recreation, and cultural enrichment.
Review program plans, conduct observations, and provide coaching and feedback to staff to ensure high-quality instruction and participant engagement.
Support the Program Director in creating opportunities for participants to share their interests, influence program activities, assume leadership roles, and provide meaningful feedback on their program experience.
Foster an inclusive, welcoming, and supportive environment that meets the diverse needs, abilities, identities, and interests of participants, and collaborate with the Inclusion Coordinator and other designated staff to ensure appropriate accommodations and meaningful participation for all youth.
Assist with continuous quality improvement efforts, including corrective action plans, monitoring follow-up, and implementation of program enhancements.

Staff Supervision and Development

Provide supervision, guidance, scheduling support, and daily oversight to frontline staff, interns, and volunteers, ensuring adequate staffing coverage and compliance with required participant-to-staff ratios.
Assist with staff recruitment, onboarding, training, professional development, and performance management.
Monitor staff attendance, preparedness, professional conduct, and compliance with organizational and regulatory requirements.
Support coaching, documentation, and corrective action processes as needed.
Ensure staff understand and adhere to safety procedures, mandated-reporting requirements, and participant supervision expectations.

Participant Engagement, Attendance, and Family Partnerships

Monitor participant enrollment, attendance, participation, and retention to ensure compliance with contractual requirements and achievement of program enrollment and participation goals.
Oversee the accurate collection, review, and timely entry of attendance and enrollment data, regularly monitoring attendance trends, absenteeism, lateness, and participation rates, and addressing discrepancies or areas of concern.
Develop and implement strategies to improve participant engagement, attendance, and retention, including outreach to families, follow-up regarding absences or inconsistent attendance, identification of barriers to participation, and implementation of re-engagement strategies.
Support recruitment, enrollment, orientation, and retention efforts, maintaining accurate enrollment records, participant files, and waitlists, and ensuring enrollment and rate-of-participation requirements are met.
Establish and maintain positive relationships with participants and families by communicating program expectations, attendance requirements, participant progress, upcoming events, and available support services; responding to questions and concerns; and elevating significant issues as appropriate.
Support family engagement initiatives, including orientations, workshops, conferences, celebrations, and other program events that strengthen participant and family connections.
Collaborate with school personnel, community partners, and service providers to support participant success, align program activities with school-day priorities, expand resources and opportunities for participants and families, and facilitate referrals when additional support is needed.
Prepare and share attendance, enrollment, and participation reports with program leadership and recommend strategies to strengthen participant engagement, retention, and overall program outcomes.

Safety, Behavior Support, and Incident Response

Ensure the safety, well-being, and active supervision of participants throughout all program activities, including arrivals, transitions, field trips, special events, and dismissal.
Implement and reinforce positive behavior-management and restorative practices that promote a supportive, inclusive, and respectful program environment.
Respond promptly and appropriately to behavioral incidents, injuries, medical concerns, family complaints, and emergencies, ensuring timely communication with program leadership and required stakeholders.
Ensure incidents are properly documented, reported, and resolved in accordance with organizational policies, DYCD requirements, and mandated-reporting obligations.
Support emergency preparedness efforts, including drills, evacuation procedures, crisis response protocols, and staff training.
Maintain the confidentiality and appropriate handling of participant medical, behavioral, emergency, and accommodation-related information, and support the safe planning and execution of field trips and off-site activities.

Data Management and Administrative Support

Maintain accurate, organized, and confidential program records, including attendance, enrollment, incident documentation, family communications, staff compliance records, and other required program documentation.
Ensure timely and accurate data entry, reporting, and recordkeeping to support contract compliance, program monitoring, audits, licensing reviews, regulatory requirements, and organizational reporting needs.
Assist with administrative and operational functions, including staff scheduling, supply and inventory management, purchasing, timesheet review, and resource allocation.
Support the planning and coordination of special events, field trips, family engagement activities, showcases, and other program initiatives, ensuring alignment with the approved program calendar and established deadlines.
Participate in supervisory meetings, DYCD trainings, technical-assistance sessions, and professional development opportunities, and perform other duties as assigned by the Program Director or department leadership.

World Wildlife Fund (WWF), one of the world’s leading conservation organizations, seeks a Managing Director, WWF Impact.

Major Function

WWF Impact is a dedicated investment function effort that sits within the Nature Finance and Investment (NFI) team. The Managing Director will oversee all of WWF Impact’s activities, which include initiating and managing partnerships with external sustainable investment asset managers and managing an evolving portfolio of direct equity investments into start-ups that further our conservation mission. The Managing Director will manage a highly skilled team of conservation investment professionals in pursuit of successful high impact partnerships and private investment opportunities. The Managing Director will serve on the leadership team of the broader NFI team and will have primary responsibility for managing WWF Impact’s relationships, internally and externally in the market.

Key Responsibilities

Leadership and Strategic Direction: Lead WWF Impact, the dedicated team within NFI where we pursue both direct early stage (catalytic) investing opportunities as well as external partnerships with asset manager partnerships in which WWF serves the role of impact advisor.
Asset Manager Partnerships: Oversee the process to forge new asset manager partnership opportunities through effective partner identification, collaboration, diligence, and project / fund development. Work with the WWF Impact team, NFI Management, and WWF programmatic teams to pursue and close high potential asset management partnerships in priority sectors (regenerative agriculture, blue oceans, sustainable infrastructure, circular economy, carbon finance, etc.). Ensure that investment memorandums are well-prepared and uphold a rigorous standard for investment and impact analyses. Lead the investment team in presentations and deliberations in internal governance processes.

Resource Mobilization: Develop, maintain and advance key internal and external relationships for partnership success. Management: Oversee a growing team of professionals within the WWF Impact team. Manage WWF Impact’s budget and build capacity of both WWF US and Country Office staff in support of NFI’s goal of significant capital mobilization to conservation finance.

Taíno CoLAB Academy NH | Opening September 2027 

ABOUT TAÍNO CoLAB ACADEMY 

Taíno CoLAB Academy is a public charter high school opening in New Haven, CT in September 2027. Rooted in the Taíno community's history and New Haven's vibrant Latino heritage, Taíno CoLAB is designed as a Community School 2.0
— genuinely embedded in, accountable to, and in reciprocal relationship with its community. 

Academically, Taíno CoLAB operates through the 4D Quantum Learning Matrix
— CoLAB Education's signature framework for future-ready, student-centered learning across four interconnected dimensions: Inquiry, Design, Creativity, and Service. Students don't just learn about the world — they investigate it, design within it, create across it, and serve through it.  

We are not a traditional school with innovative add-ons. We are a fundamentally different kind of school. We are looking for a Director of Operations who is energized by that distinction. 

THE ROLE 

The Director of Operations of Taíno CoLAB Academy is the school's chief operational and administrative leader
— responsible for translating the CoLAB vision into robust, equitable, and seamless operational systems that support students, teachers, families, and community partners.

This is not a purely administrative desk job. The Director of Operations builds the structural backbone of a learning community
. They work in close partnership with the Founding Executive Director, the Founding Director of Academics, and CoLAB Education's leadership team. Reports to: Executive Director.

SYSTEMS OWNERSHIP 

The Director of Operations owns the following systems — accountable for their design, implementation, and continuous improvement: 

1. Financial Management and Budgeting System

Design and manage the school's operating budget in alignment with strategic priorities. Oversee accounts payable/receivable, payroll processing, grant management, and audit preparation. Ensure financial transparency, compliance with state and federal regulations, and fiduciary stewardship of public funds.

2. Facilities, Safety, and Capital Infrastructure System

Oversee the leasing, design, maintenance, and safety compliance of the school's physical plant. Create a warm, welcoming, and secure physical environment that reflects the school's identity as a community resource. Manage facilities vendors, emergency preparedness drills, security systems, and custodial operations.

3. Technology, Data, and Information Systems

Manage all educational and operational technology infrastructure, hardware deployment, and software licensing. Ensure secure student data privacy compliance (FERPA, state standards). Oversee the Student Information System (SIS) and provide operational data support for enrollment, attendance, and reporting.

4. Compliance, Governance, and Legal Operations

Manage charter accountability reporting, state and federal compliance filings, board operations support, and legal risk management. Ensure adherence to health, safety, nutritional, transportation, and special education compliance frameworks.

5. People Management System

Manage onboarding, benefits administration, credentialing tracking, and HR compliance for all school staff. Support the Director of Academics and Executive Director with recruitment logistics, personnel recordkeeping, and staff culture initiatives from an operational lens.

6. School Operations and Logistics Partnership

Partner with the Director of Academics on daily school operations, student transportation, food service delivery, student registration, and family communications. Ensure operational priorities actively serve instructional goals — never the reverse.

EXPECTED APPROACHES

Lead as a Learner 

The Director of Operations is a chief learner in operational excellence — not an immovable expert. They model curiosity about how systems run, ask operational and front-line staff questions before imposing solutions, and credit the team's ideas. They are the first to test a new process, workflow, or software protocol and the first to reflect on what isn't working smoothly for teachers, students, or families.

Facilitate, Don't Dictate 

The Director of Operations leads through service and collaboration. They listen to the needs of educators and families, using feedback loops to continuously refine operational processes and remove barriers.

Center Community Voice Structurally 

Operations must reflect the community's values. The Director of Operations ensures that families experience welcoming, accessible, and culturally responsive administrative interactions from registration to daily engagement.

Hold Equity as the Core Standard 

The Director of Operations understands that operational equity means resource allocation and service delivery prioritize the students and communities most often underserved by traditional institutions.

Think in 4D 

The framework applies to operations, too. Every operational workflow is evaluated through the lens of Inquiry, Design, Creativity, and Service to ensure the school's infrastructure mirrors its innovative pedagogical model.

Model Adaptive Confidence 

Leading a founding school requires comfort in ambiguity and rapid iteration. The Director of Operations makes sound decisions with incomplete information, communicates transparently about operational hurdles, and embraces mistakes as data points for system improvement.

Requirements And Preferences

The Broward County Board of County Commissioners, Transportation Department
is seeking qualified candidates for the position of
Chief Operating Officer (Assistant Director of Transportation) in its Operations Division.

The Community

Bordering Southeast Florida’s Atlantic coastline, Broward County is the seventeenth most populous county in the nation and the second largest in the state of Florida. Home to over 1.9 million people, Broward County is located between Palm Beach and Miami-Dade counties, forming the center of South Florida’s largest metropolitan area in which 6.1 million people reside. Within the County’s approximate 1,200 square miles are 31 municipalities, the largest of which is the county seat, Fort Lauderdale. About two-thirds of Broward County is part of the undeveloped Everglades conservation area. Broward County boasts 23 miles of pristine Atlantic coastline, and its beaches attract both the local population as well as tourists from around the world. With an average year-round temperature of 76 degrees, Broward County has a tropical climate and is a choice destination for over nineteen million visitors every year.

Broward County’s warm climate, demographic diversity, robust and expanding economy, top-rated schools, colleges and universities, cutting-edge healthcare, and an advanced transportation system afford its residents an exceptional quality of life. Broward offers world-class dining, high-quality theater, cosmopolitan nightlife, and premium shopping venues, as well as an abundance of recreational activities such as golf, pickleball, soccer, deep-sea fishing, boating and vast opportunities for fun on the beach.

The Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport is in Broward County and is less than two miles from Port Everglades where most major cruise lines use as a homeport. Among Broward County’s abundant retail shopping options is Sawgrass Mills, the largest one-story value retail shopping mall in the United States. For the sports enthusiast, Broward County is home to the National Hockey League’s Florida Panthers, while the National Basketball Association’s Miami Heat, the Major League Baseball’s Miami Marlins, and the National Football League’s Miami Dolphins are just a short drive or quick train ride away.

The County Government

The Broward County government was established under Charter in 1975 as a home-rule government. The County has a Council/Manager form of government. The Broward County Board of County Commissioners is composed of nine members, elected every two years for four-year staggered terms. Commissioners are voted to the position by their district constituents through partisan elections. The Mayor and Vice-Mayor are Commission members annually elected by the Commission for one-year terms. The Commission appoints the County Administrator, the County Attorney, and the County Auditor.

The County Administrator serves as the Chief Executive Officer and manages the County’s six major operating departments: Transportation, Aviation, Finance and Administrative Services, Human Services, Port Everglades, and Public Works and Environmental Services; eight offices and three divisions, which all together comprise over 70 lines of business.

The County has nearly 6,700 employees and eight organized bargaining units. The County budget for FY26 is $8.75 billion of which $5.45 billion is Operating, $2.55 billion is Capital and $0.76 billion is Debt Service. The budget reflects strategic investments in transit, the seaport and airport, and many other critical services to residents.

Broward County Department of Transportation

The Broward County Transportation Department is comprised of a comprehensive transportation network that ensures the safe, secure and efficient movement of its citizens.

The existing public transportation network provides approximately 26 million fixed route and express service bus trips annually. In addition, the organization is adding over 200 miles of premium service through its Premium Mobility (PREMO) plan. Under PREMO, BCT is transitioning from a bus only organization to a full multi-modal provider of public transportation with heavy rail, light rail, bus rapid transit, and high frequency bus service thus reducing the reliance on single-occupancy vehicles and helping to alleviate traffic congestion. The integration of these premium public transportation services will ensure seamless connectivity between bus services and other transit options.

BCT works closely with federal, state, and local governments, regional agencies and the community at large to address transportation needs and priorities. Moving forward BCT will have an enhanced level of long-term planning and coordination with the numerous government organizations, such as the Federal Transit Administration (FTA), Federal Railroad Administration (FRA), Transportation Security Administration (TSA), Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), Florida Department of Transportation State Safety Oversight Office and the Broward County Metropolitan Planning Organization. By leveraging federal, state, and local funding, the department is able to implement innovative solutions and infrastructure improvements, enhancing the overall quality of life for Broward County residents.

The Position

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) provides leadership and direction for the Transportation Department's Operations Division, including bus, rail, paratransit, on-board systems, and fleet services. Responsibilities include executive oversight, operational management, financial performance, strategic planning, employee development, safety promotion, customer advocacy, and coordination of assigned division activities. This is a 24/7 operation.

Blue Star Families

Blue Star Families is the largest nonprofit dedicated to making military life better for families. Each year, we support over 1.5 million military- and veteran-connected family members through a national network of 300,000+ members and local chapters in communities across the country.

Our mission is simple and bold: We make military life awesome for families.

We listen, share, partner, and act to deliver evidence-based, data-driven solutions that work for real people. We’re a lifestyle organization, a friend and neighbor, and a trusted partner. Our approach is collaborative, human-centered, and designed with the whole family in mind.

A Blue Star Family is one with an immediate family member — a spouse, parent, or child — actively serving in the U.S. Armed Forces, including the Guard and Reserves. These families face unique challenges: frequent relocations, deployments, career disruption, and isolation. We respond with research-informed programs that create connection, build resilience, and foster a true sense of belonging.

We serve with urgency but build trust over time — because change happens at the speed of trust. Whether we’re driving spouse employment, supporting caregivers, or helping communities welcome military families, we strive for upstream solutions.

Who We’re Looking For

Bold thinkers. Fast movers. Smart collaborators. People who want to build, lead, and drive measurable change — and who care deeply about making an impact that matters.

What You’ll Do Here

Solve complex challenges with data, heart, and humility
Build cross-sector partnerships that get things done
Help military families feel at home wherever they live

If you're ready to work in a high-performance, mission-driven environment — and to make life better for those who serve — Blue Star Families is where you belong.

General Description

The Associate Director, Development for the Utah Chapter is responsible for assisting in local fundraising efforts, cultivating donor relationships, and supporting the development of strategic partnerships to support the chapter’s financial sustainability and growth. This role partners closely with the Chapter Executive Director and the national Development team to align local fundraising strategies with Blue Star Families’ mission and organizational goals.

The Associate Director will steward a portfolio of individual, corporate, and foundation donors and support grant writing and reporting in collaboration with the national team.

While this role is remote, periodic out-of-town, overnight travel is an essential function. In-person time is critical to how we work — enabling deep collaboration, team alignment, creative problem-solving, and a shared sense of purpose. Team members are expected to travel several times per year for offsites, planning sessions, and company-wide gatherings. These events are essential for contributing to team outcomes, building trust across the organization, and staying aligned in a distributed environment. Participation in these in-person gatherings is a required part of the role and integral to successful performance in our remote-first organization.

The Associate Director must reside in the local community the Chapter serves. Preference will be given to candidates who have resided in the designated Chapter community for a minimum of the past three years.

Key Job Functions

Assist the Executive Director with the local fundraising strategy to meet or exceed chapter revenue goals.
Meet or exceed an annual fundraising goal of at least $100,000.
Build, qualify, and actively manage a portfolio of at least 30 new major gift prospects (distinct from existing pipelines), with responsibility for identifying, cultivating, and advancing these individuals through the full donor lifecycle toward solicitation and long-term engagement
Cultivate, solicit, and steward relationships with individual donors, corporate sponsors, and foundations.
Collaborate with the Executive Director and national Development team to identify and pursue funding opportunities aligned with chapter programs and goals.
Collaborate with the Executive Director on donor recognition and ensure consistent, high-quality communication with funders and supporters.
Support the development and execution of donor engagement events and activities.
Maintain accurate donor records and activity tracking in CRM (e.g., Salesforce).
Assist with grant proposal writing and reporting.
Partner with local program staff to align fundraising with community impact.
Represent Blue Star Families at Chapter sponsored events, community events, and networking opportunities to elevate the chapter’s visibility and mission.
Perform other duties as assigned

Required Experience, Skills & Background

Minimum 5-7 years of relevant experience in fundraising for a nonprofit organization
Demonstrated success in individual giving, corporate sponsorships, and/or grant writing.
Strong relationship-building and communication skills.
Self-starter with the ability to work both independently and collaboratively.
Experience with CRM software (e.g., Salesforce).
Local travel requirements required outside of your home office will be up to 40% or less depending on business needs.
Ability to travel out of town overnight several times per year for staff offsites, planning retreats, and company-wide events. These gatherings are essential for connection, brainstorming, and staying strategically aligned across teams. Participation is required as a core part of the role.
May be required to work nights, weekends, and holidays as necessary to carry out key job functions.

Desired Experience, Skills & Background

Bachelor’s degree preferred
Knowledge of the military family experience
Familiarity with membership-driven organizations

More About Blue Star Families

Blue Star Families empowers military and Veteran families to thrive by connecting them with their civilian neighbors — both people and organizations — to create strong communities of mutual support. We believe we're all stronger when we take care of one another.

Our groundbreaking research is raising the nation's awareness of the unique challenges of military family life. With the help of neighbors across the country, Blue Star Families is overcoming the isolation and alienation of frequent moves, deployments, and reduced support from the government. Our innovative programs are solving specific challenges for military families, including fighting economic insecurity with resources that foster spouse career development, creating family strength with rich family programming, and providing critical peer support for caregivers, whose numbers are only increasing.

Blue Star Families is a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization.
